content:
OpenAI is introducing a new way for ChatGPT and Codex to learn and remember your Mac activity, even when it happens outside of apps.

ChatGPT Computer History is an upgraded replacement for the earlier Chronicle research preview for Codex

The all-new Computer History feature builds a searchable timeline from activity across selected apps and websites.

OpenAI announced Computer History in a Thursday desktop app changelog. The feature is off by default and must be enabled by users, letting them decide which sources are included in the record.

The update builds on Codex being added to the ChatGPT desktop app a month ago and follows OpenAI's experimental Chronicle feature released earlier this year.

OpenAI said Computer History is effectively replacing the Chronicle research preview, but stressed it is a rebuild rather than a simple rename.

Chronicle relied on screenshots; Computer History instead uses macOS accessibility-recorded interactions — clicks, keystrokes, keyboard shortcuts, and switching between apps.

Here's OpenAI's description of the new feature:

Computer History is an opt-in feature in the ChatGPT macOS desktop app that turns app and website activity into a memory and timeline for ChatGPT and Codex. Users can choose which apps and sites to include, pause collection at any time, and view or delete records. Computer History is now available to ChatGPT Pro, Business, and Enterprise users. Business and Enterprise admins must first enable the relevant permissions before workspace members can turn it on. Initial availability excludes the European Economic Area (EEA), Switzerland, and the UK.

OpenAI also explained how eligible users can enable this opt-in feature, Computer History:

Users can ask what they were doing before a break, find a recently viewed document, or generate a summary of the day's work. ChatGPT may also proactively suggest turning repeated workflows into skills or automations.

Computer History and privacy

OpenAI said ChatGPT's Computer History feature does not capture screenshots, screen recordings, microphone input, or system audio; private browsing activity is likewise not collected.

Users can view timeline items in Settings, reveal individual memory files in Finder, delete specific items, or clear activity from the past 10 minutes, one hour, one day, or all time.

Computer History temporarily stores interaction events on the Mac for up to 48 hours. OpenAI said those events are processed on its servers to generate memories, but are not retained after processing and are not used to train models. The resulting plain-text memory files are stored locally until the user deletes them.

OpenAI also warned that Computer History could increase the risk of prompt injection from malicious content inside apps or websites. The company recommends users pause activity collection when communicating with others without their explicit consent, and exclude apps that handle sensitive information.

For more information on the opt-in Computer History feature in ChatGPT for Mac, go here.
